messages.subject: bfactor()

Hello Phil (and the users),

We are working on bfactor() function to fit a general factor and six different specific factors. 

The factor indicators in our original data are not dichotomous or 0/1/2, but that can go up higher e.g., from zero to 26 for some items.

Then bfactor() function gives the following message: 

"Item re-scored so that all values are within a distance of 1"

Can anyone help on what is the re-scoring approach and/or how the re-scored data can be returned ? 

Best regards 

Jung Yeon

On Sat, Dec 14, 2019 at 7:13 AM JYP <saty...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,

We are working on bfactor() function to fit a general factor and six different specific factors. 

The factor indicators in our original data are not dichotomous or 0/1/2, but that can go up higher e.g., from zero to 26 for some items.

If your indicator variables have 26 unique values you might want to treat the response data as continuous and use something like the lavaan package instead. Treating this many observations as discrete is going to chew up a lot of degrees of freedom and introduce many issues related to count sparceneess.  HTH.

Phil
